originalTitle: $20 billion bet: Where is Warren Buffett's successor spending Berkshire's cash pile after 14 quarters?
simplifiedContent: Warren Buffett's company, Berkshire Hathaway, has started buying more stocks than it's selling for the first time in 14 quarters. The new CEO, Greg Abel, spent almost $20 billion on buying new stocks and $4.5 billion on buying back Berkshire's own shares in the second quarter. This is a big change for the company, and it's putting its money into well-known companies like Apple and Alphabet (the company that owns Google). The company's top investments now include these familiar names, which could be a sign of where the CEO thinks the market is headed. This matters because Berkshire Hathaway is a large and influential investor, and its actions can impact the overall stock market.

originalTitle: Rs 7,681 crore IPO rush next week: Shiprocket, Milky Mist among 9 issues to hit the market
simplifiedContent: Next week, nine companies, including Shiprocket and Milky Mist Dairy Food, are planning to raise a total of Rs 7,681 crore by issuing new shares to the public, known as an Initial Public Offering (IPO). This means that people can buy shares of these companies for the first time. The IPOs will start on August 10 and 12, which is a busy time for the stock market. This is important because it gives investors a chance to put their money into new companies, and it also shows that these companies are growing and need more funds. The companies that launched their IPOs last week will also start trading their shares on the stock market soon.

originalTitle: Berkshire Hathaway spends down cash pile under CEO Greg Abel
simplifiedContent: Berkshire Hathaway, a big company led by CEO Greg Abel, used some of the money it had saved up, reducing its cash reserves to $365.5 billion. The company spent $4.5 billion buying back its own shares and nearly $20 billion investing in other companies, such as Alphabet and Taylor Morrison. This means that Berkshire Hathaway is putting its money to work instead of just letting it sit in the bank. The company's operating earnings, which is a measure of how well its businesses are doing, increased by 16% to almost $13 billion, even though its insurance business didn't do as well as expected. This is important because it shows that the company is actively using its resources to try to make more money.

originalTitle: Defence stock Apollo Micro Systems declares Q1 results 2026. Revenue jumps 88% YoY to  ₹251 crore, PAT up 43%
simplifiedContent: Apollo Micro Systems, a company that makes products for the defence industry, just announced its financial results for the first quarter of 2026. The company's revenue, or the amount of money it made from selling its products, increased by 88% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹251.3 crore. Its net profit, which is the amount of money it made after paying all its expenses, also increased by 43% to ₹25.2 crore. This is a significant improvement and suggests that the company is doing well. This matters because it indicates the company's financial health and performance, which can affect its stock price and attractiveness to investors.

originalTitle: Q1 results 2026: Vodafone Idea to RVNL among companies to declare Q1 results next week; check full list here
simplifiedContent: Next week, several well-known companies will announce their financial results for the first quarter of 2026. This means they will share how much money they made and lost from January to March. Companies like Vodafone Idea, Tata Motors, and Bharat Forge are on the list, and this information can help investors decide whether to buy or sell their stocks. These results can give investors an idea of how well each company is doing and whether they are making progress. Checking these results can be important for investors who want to make informed decisions about their investments.

originalTitle: Multibagger stock to be in focus on Monday; here's why
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: A certain stock, known as a "multibagger" (meaning it has increased in value many times over), will be closely watched on Monday. This stock slightly went up in value on Friday, increasing by 0.43% to ₹46.92 per share. This means that people who own this stock saw a small gain at the end of the trading day on Friday. The fact that it's a multibagger stock makes it interesting to investors, who will be paying attention to it on Monday to see what happens next. This matters because investors want to know if the stock will continue to go up or down in value.
